items.title: Marian McPartland interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, April 26, 1997
items.q: we had a George — oh God isn’t this awful, I mean he’s a local drummer, a very good drummer, and we just played tune after tune after tune.

ctx.x: So, here’s an imaginary young lady, she’s 20, and you happen to meet her somewhere, and she says, “Marian, I really want to make a living as a jazz piano player.” Would you suggest that she think of something else to do, or what would you say to her?

Well I probably would say well can you play, do you have a piano, who do you listen to, can you play? And if I’m in a room, well play me something. Have you taken lessons? You know I don’t want somebody that hasn’t done anything, I mean they have to sort of have an idea about it. Once in a while I get somebody, some dilettante will say, “well I don’t really want to take piano lessons, I just want to play a few chords like George © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
Shearing.” And I say, “well you can’t do that. There’s no way you could. You’ve got to do the whole thing or nothing.”
